subject: SOC 2 Type II: request for narrow control samples, MFA/session slices & bridge letter
messages:
From: Amelia Ramos <amelia.ramos@novushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 Type II report + targeted control artifacts request

Marcus —

We are kicking off our SOC 2 Type II review and need the latest report plus a few targeted control artifacts that fall outside of the standard report scope. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide the following: 

- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent period) and a bridge letter covering the period overlap if a formal report delivery will miss our audit window.
- MFA rotation/validation history for privileged accounts (we’re primarily interested in changes to admin accounts between 2026-06-01 and 2026-08-31).
- Privileged access review artifacts (access recertification logs or reviewer attestations) for the same window.
- Session/authentication log slices for the audit window above (authentication successes/failures, SSO assertions, and token issuance traces), with guidance on pseudonymization applied to user identifiers.

Also: what delivery mechanisms do you support for sensitive artifacts? SFTP, secure S3 presigned link, or vendor portal? We’ll need an estimate on how long extracts will take and whether you can provide a manifest of files so our auditors can reference specific artifacts.

Can you loop in your security/compliance lead and share an expected timeline? Our audit kickoff is next week, so a 3–5 business day turnaround for targeted slices would be ideal.

Thanks,
Amelia Ramos
Senior Security Analyst
Novus Health
amelia.ramos@novushealth.com


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Ramos <amelia.ramos@novushealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report + targeted control artifacts request

Amelia —

Thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely support the request; I’ve looped in Laura (security/compliance) and Olga (controls evidence) to coordinate extracts and bridge wording. High-level next steps: 

1) I’ll confirm availability of the Type II report and whether a bridge letter is necessary (we typically provide a bridge letter when the Type II period does not fully cover a customer audit window).
2) Olga will prepare a manifest and propose a secure delivery method (we can do presigned S3 links or SFTP; we do not use a public vendor portal for sensitive logs).
3) Laura will scope the exact slices for MFA/privileged-review and confirm pseudonymization approach (hashed email vs. irreversible token).

Quick clarifying Qs to help us scope the extracts: 
- Confirm audit window = 2026-06-01 → 2026-08-31 (you mentioned that range above).
- For privileged account history: do you need the full rotation history (all rotations/credential changes) or a sampling of privileged user changes (e.g., 5–10 most active privileged accounts)?
- For session traces: do auditors require token-level traces (raw token issue IDs) or a summarized auth event record (timestamp, event_type, pseudonymized_user_id, client_id, ip)?

If you prefer, we can draft a bridge letter and attach a manifest for your review within 24 hours, then deliver log slices within 3 business days after we get your confirmation on sampling.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Lead — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com


From: Amelia Ramos <amelia.ramos@novushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@novushealth.com
Date: 2026-10-01T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report + targeted control artifacts request

Thanks Marcus — that plan works. A few clarifications: 

- Confirmed audit window: 2026-06-01 to 2026-08-31.
- Privileged account history: we prefer a complete history of privileged admin account rotations and elevation events for that window (if the full set is very large, a justified sampling is acceptable but call it out in the manifest).
- Session traces: auditors typically want token-level traces for a handful of sessions to validate session handling and token revocation flows — at minimum we need token issue/refresh/revoke events for five distinct sessions across two privileged accounts. If you need to hash identifiers, please describe the hashing algorithm and salt handling in your manifest.
- Delivery: SFTP is preferred for our team (we can provide host + credentials). If Redwood prefers presigned S3, confirm expiry windows and transfer encryption.

I’ve attached our evidence request form (Novus_control_request_form.xlsx) to capture which artifacts map to which SOC 2 CC controls — please populate the form and return it with the manifest. Also: our HubSpot record ID for this renewal is 005624.

If you can get a bridge letter draft and manifest by EOD today, we’ll prioritize review and send SFTP details first thing tomorrow.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — our auditors are waiting.

-Amelia

Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report + targeted control artifacts request — bridge draft & export plan attached

Amelia —

Attached is a draft bridge letter (redwood_bridge_letter_draft.pdf) and a proposed manifest (authn_log_manifest.csv) that outlines the planned extracts. I’ve also included export_instructions.txt with our preferred S3 presigned workflow and SFTP fallback details. Summary / commitments below: 

- SOC 2 Type II: We will confirm availability of the formal report by EOD; if the most recent Type II does not fully cover your audit window, we will finalize and sign the attached bridge letter.
- Log extracts: Olga will produce the requested session/token traces and privileged-account rotation history scoped to 2026-06-01 → 2026-08-31. Expect the first manifest-backed delivery via presigned S3 links within 3 business days after we receive the completed Novus_control_request_form.xlsx (you can return it to me or upload to the Drive link we shared).
- Pseudonymization: Our standard approach is salted SHA-256 hashing of user IDs with a rotating per-export salt; the manifest includes an entry describing the hash function and salt retention policy. If you need irreversible tokenization or a specific HMAC, note that in the returned form and we will adjust.
- Sampling: we will include the full privileged rotation events unless the export size exceeds the threshold in the manifest column; if so, we’ll provide a deterministic sample (seeded) and note the sampling algorithm for auditor repeatability.

Next actions for Novus: 
1) Return Novus_control_request_form.xlsx populated with any changes & preferred delivery (SFTP vs S3).
2) Confirm whether token-level traces for the five sessions should include raw JWT IDs (we can include them but recommend redaction in transit).

We’ll keep Laura on the thread for compliance attestations and Olga for the technical export.

Best regards,
Marcus Lin
Account Lead — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Attachments referenced: redwood_bridge_letter_draft.pdf (draft), authn_log_manifest.csv (manifest of planned files + sample sizes), export_instructions.txt (delivery options & encryption details)
